title: Edge0: a 35-billion-parameter model in 3 GB of memory

facts.description: Streaming MoE inference: SSD expert offload, Recover-LoRA and prerouter routing prediction (README)
facts.memory: about 2.9 GiB MLX allocator peak for edge0-35b, short contexts, on a Mac mini M4 Pro 24 GB (README). The repo description says about 2.5 GB; use the README figure.
facts.speed: 14.9 to 17.7 tokens per second for edge0-35b on the same Mac mini (README)
facts.quality: MMLU-Pro 81.0 for edge0-35b (int4) vs 84.6 for Qwen3.6-35B-A3B (fp16), authors' own OpenCompass run (README)
facts.requirements: Python version needs macOS on Apple Silicon with MLX; disk about 23 GB for the 35B weights (README)
facts.media_plan: README logo assets/20260908-223115.jpg; a Mac run must be built from the repo before render

verify_before_render: The memory figure is the README's 2.9 GiB, on a 24 GB Mac mini; say 'about 3 GB' only.
Benchmarks are the authors' own; keep the attribution on screen.
A real run on an Apple Silicon Mac must confirm speed before render.
Capture pack repo-edge0-01 must be built before render.

scenes.heading: 35B MODEL IN 3 GB OF MEMORY
scenes.sub: Edge0 · streams from SSD on a Mac
scenes.say: A local AI model: 35 billion parameters in 3 GB of memory.

scenes.heading: Edge0
scenes.sub: keeps the model on the SSD, loads only what it needs
scenes.say: It's called Edge0. It keeps the model on your SSD and loads only the parts it needs for the next step.

scenes.heading: WHAT IT NEEDS
scenes.say: The Python version runs on Apple Silicon Macs. You download the 23 gigabyte model, then run it with the included scripts.

scenes.heading: ABOUT 15 TO 18 TOKENS A SECOND
scenes.say: On a Mac mini M4 Pro with 24 gigabytes, the 35-billion model runs at about 15 to 18 tokens per second.

scenes.heading: THE CATCH
scenes.say: It's a preview. In the authors' own test, it scores 81 on MMLU-Pro, against 84.6 for the full-precision base model.
Would you run a 35-billion model on your laptop? Comment EDGE and I'll pin the link.
